title: Four Individuals Charged After Extensive $48 Million Fraud Investigation
content:
Posted on:
Tuesday June 16
Location:
Waterloo
Occurrence #:
WA20264188
Waterloo Regional Police Service’s Commercial Fraud Unit has completed a complex, multi-year investigation into a large-scale financial fraud involving a local firearms and ammunition distribution business and a commercial financing company.
Between 2016 and 2020, the distribution business secured tens of millions of dollars in financing through forged business documents. The fraud was uncovered in 2020 during financial audits which revealed serious financial irregularities and resulted in bankruptcy proceedings.
Investigators found that many of the transactions the business reported had never actually occurred. They also uncovered fabricated communications and deliberate misrepresentations designed to make the operation appear legitimate in order to obtain funding.
Nearly 20,000 fraudulent invoices were submitted in total, leading to an estimated $48 million in losses.
As a result of the investigation by WRPS’ Commercial Fraud Unit, a 52-year-old male and a 48-year-old female from London, a 56-year-old male from South Frontenac, and a 64-year-old male from Guelph have been arrested and jointly charged with:
Fraud Over $5,000
Forgery
Uttering Forged Documents
Falsification of Business Documents
Additional charges include Possession of Property Obtained by Crime, Laundering Proceeds of Crime, and Identity Fraud.
The accused parties are scheduled to appear in court at a later date.

title: Waterloo Regional Police Launch Initiative Targeting Scrap Metal and Wire Thefts in Cambridge
content:
Posted on:
Wednesday June 17
Location:
Cambridge
Waterloo Regional Police are launching a proactive initiative in Cambridge to address an increase in thefts involving scrap metal, copper wire, and other materials from businesses and construction sites.
The initiative, led by the South Division Crime Suppression, Analysis, and Response (CSAR) Unit, will run from June 17 to July 8, 2026. Officers will focus on prevention, enforcement, and education in locations identified through crime analysis.
Between February 4 and May 30, 2026, Waterloo Regional Police investigated 38 incidents involving scrap metal or wire thefts across Cambridge. These incidents have primarily occurred overnight and on weekends in industrial and construction areas across Cambridge, particularly in the north end and Galt areas.
Targets have included commercial properties under renovation, construction sites, homes under construction, metal recycling businesses, and power equipment stores. In several incidents, suspects have also targeted telecommunications infrastructure, cutting wire from Bell lines at multiple locations, resulting in estimated losses and damages in the hundreds of thousands of dollars.
Stolen items have included copper wiring, scrap metal, tools, and wiring removed from heating and cooling systems.
Investigations indicate suspects are using a variety of methods to gain access, including entering fenced compounds, cutting locks on sea cans, prying doors and windows, and even damaging structures to create entry points. Once inside, suspects often remove wire and metal materials quickly due to their resale value and ease of transport.
“These thefts are often opportunistic and occur when materials are left unsecured, visible, or accessible, particularly after hours,” said Staff Sergeant Jay MacSween of WRPS’ South Division CSAR Unit.
As part of the initiative, officers will be conducting proactive patrols and targeted enforcement in identified problem areas. They will also be visiting businesses, construction sites, and industrial locations to share information about current trends and provide practical crime prevention advice.
Police are encouraging businesses and site operators to take steps to reduce the risk of theft, including:
Securing materials in locked buildings, containers, or fenced compounds
Keeping valuable items out of public view
Posting clearly visible No Trespassing signage
Installing and maintaining video surveillance systems
Ensuring adequate lighting around storage areas and entry points
Restricting access to sites and securing gates and locks
Marking materials where possible and conducting regular inventory checks
Timely reporting remains critical. Police are urging the public and business owners to report suspicious activity and thefts as soon as possible, as surveillance footage and witness information can assist investigations and support enforcement efforts.
Anyone with information is encouraged to contact Waterloo Regional Police at 519-570-9777 or submit a tip anonymously through Crime Stoppers at 1‑800‑222‑8477 or online at
www.waterloocrimestoppers.com

title: Waterloo Regional Police Service and Municipal Partners Introduce Dedicated By-law Phone Number
content:
Posted on:
Wednesday June 17
Location:
Waterloo Region
The Waterloo Regional Police Service (WRPS), in partnership with the cities of Kitchener, Waterloo, and Cambridge, and the Township of North Dumfries, is introducing a new dedicated by-law phone number to improve how residents report by-law concerns across Waterloo Region.
The new centralized phone number will provide residents with a direct and efficient way to report issues such as property standards concerns, noise complaints, and parking by-law matters, without competing with police emergency or non-emergency calls.
Currently, by-law calls requiring a 24/7 response are routed through police non-emergency lines and managed through police communications systems. This has contributed to increased call volumes within police communications, reduced operational efficiency, and heightened privacy concerns.
In 2025, WRPS received 9,649 by-law-related calls, averaging approximately 26 per day.
“Separating by-law and police communications is an important step forward,” said Mark Crowell, Chief of Police, for WRPS. “This change allows our Communications Centre members to focus on urgent police matters, while ensuring residents continue to receive timely and appropriate responses to by-law concerns.”
The new by-law radio channel will also enable by-law officers to communicate without using police radio systems. This separation will reduce congestion on police radio channels, prevent the sharing of non-police information over police communications, and enhance privacy protections while supporting safer and more efficient operations for both services.
The dedicated phone number will also improve data collection and reporting, enabling municipalities and WRPS to better track call volumes, response times, and resource needs for by-law enforcement.
Residents are reminded that emergencies should always be reported by calling 9-1-1. Police non-emergency matters should continue to be reported by calling 519-570-9777. Once launched, all by-law-related concerns should be directed to the new centralized by-law phone number.
The project has been approved by all four partner municipalities and supports a shared commitment to modernizing public safety and municipal services across Waterloo Region.
The new dedicated by-law phone number will go live and be shared on June 22, 2026.

title: Waterloo Regional Police Service Proud to Launch the Expanded Use of CCTV and ALPR Technology
content:
Posted on:
Tuesday June 23
Location:
Waterloo
The Waterloo Regional Police Service (WRPS) is proud to announce the expanded use of closed-circuit television (CCTV) systems equipped with automated licence plate recognition (ALPR) technology in public locations in the City of Waterloo to help prevent and investigate crime and enhance public safety.
CCTV and ALPR systems provide officers with an additional tool to support investigations and improve response to incidents. In the event of a crime or major incident, officers may review footage from these systems to gather relevant evidence from the surrounding area. The ALPR technology automatically scans licence plates and can alert officers to vehicles associated with active investigations or those reported as stolen.
Camera locations are determined through data-driven analysis conducted by the WRPS Crime Analysis Unit, focusing on areas with a demonstrated public safety need.
A list of camera locations is available on the WRPS website
. Additional locations will be added to the website as cameras are installed.
“Our goal is to enhance community safety while respecting the rights and freedoms of the community we serve,” said Chief Mark Crowell. “By using technology like CCTV and ALPR responsibly and transparently, we are providing officers with another valuable tool to help keep our community safe.”
This initiative complements WRPS’s in-car ALPR program, which was introduced in 2022.
This technology has been supported by funding from the Ministry of the Solicitor General as part of Ontario’s Guns, Gangs, and Violence Reduction Strategy. The use of CCTV with ALPR aligns with programs implemented by other police services across Ontario.
WRPS is committed to ensuring all technologies are implemented with a strong focus on privacy, accountability, and legal compliance. The collection, use, and disclosure of any information is conducted in accordance with applicable legislation, including the Criminal Code, the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms, and the Municipal Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act (MFIPPA). Footage is accessed only for legitimate law-enforcement purposes, and any video that is not required for an investigation is automatically deleted after 30 days.
The CCTV and ALPR systems will go live in Waterloo on June 23, 2026. Installation in Kitchener, Cambridge, and the Township of North Dumfries is anticipated to follow.

Waterloo Regional Police are investigating several reports of a taxi fraud scam in Waterloo.
On July 7, 2026, police received multiple reports of a taxi fraud in the University District area of Waterloo in which victims had their debit cards stolen and subsequently used fraudulently.
In each incident, a victim was approached by a female passenger inside a vehicle that appeared to be a taxi. The female advised that the driver would not accept cash payment and offered to reimburse the victim in cash if the victim paid the fare using their debit card.
During the transaction, the victim's debit card was swapped and later used to conduct fraudulent transactions.
The investigation is ongoing.
Waterloo Regional Police are encouraging members of the public to consider the following tips to help prevent being a victim of a similar scam:
Do not leave your debit or credit card unattended inside a point-of-sale terminal.
Be aware of taxi numbers and company names when using their services.
If there is an error code or the debit machine is not functioning, always remove your debit card before returning the machine for assistance.
Do not make payments for an unknown person using your personal card in exchange for cash.
Inspect your card after each transaction and ensure it is your card.
Shield the keypad when entering your PIN.
Use contactless payment options, such as tap to pay, whenever possible. No PIN is required for contactless payments.
If you have been a victim of a taxi fraud scam and have not yet reported the incident to police, please do so by calling 519-570-9777.

Thursday, July 9, 2026 1:59 p.m.
Waterloo Regional Police are warning the public about an ongoing fraud scam involving suspects posing as representatives from banks and credit card companies.
In reported incidents, victims receive phone calls from individuals claiming to be from their bank or credit card provider. The caller advises the victim that a suspicious or compromised transaction has been detected on their account and requests that they verify their card information.
To make the call appear legitimate, suspects are using spoofing technology that causes the phone number displayed on the victim's caller ID to appear as though it is originating from their financial institution.
After obtaining information from the victim, the fraudsters arrange for a courier to attend the victim's residence to collect the supposedly compromised bank or credit card. The stolen cards are then used to make fraudulent purchases.
Waterloo Regional Police would like to remind the public that legitimate banks and credit card companies will never send a courier to retrieve a compromised card and will not ask customers to disclose sensitive account information during an unsolicited phone call.
To protect yourself from becoming a victim of this scam, police recommend:
Do not provide banking, credit card, PIN, or personal information to anyone who contacts you unexpectedly.
Do not rely solely on caller ID, as phone numbers can be spoofed.
If you receive a call claiming to be from your financial institution, hang up and contact the institution directly using the phone number listed on the back of your card or on the organization's official website.
Never provide your bank or credit card to a courier or unknown individual.
Regularly monitor your accounts for unauthorized transactions.
Anyone who believes they may have been targeted by this scam is encouraged to contact their financial institution immediately and report the incident to Waterloo Regional Police at 519-570-9777.

Waterloo Regional Police Service's North Division Crime Suppression Analysis and Response Unit (CSAR) Direct Action Response Team (DART) has arrested more than 20 individuals and laid over 40 charges as part of a retail crime enforcement initiative.
Starting July 6, 2026, WRPS’ North Division Direct Action Response Team (DART) conducted a four-day retail crime enforcement initiative targeting theft, repeat offenders, and organized retail crime activities at several retail locations throughout Kitchener and Waterloo.
The focused enforcement project was launched in response to ongoing concerns from retailers regarding increasing incidents of shoplifting and organized retail theft impacting businesses across the Region. Working closely with loss prevention personnel and retail partners, officers conducted proactive enforcement operations aimed at identifying offenders, disrupting criminal activity, and enhancing public safety.
As a result of the initiative:
23 individuals were arrested
More than 40 criminal charges were laid, including Theft Under $5,000 and Possession of Stolen Property Under $5,000
Approximately $1,450 in stolen merchandise was recovered
Several prolific and repeat offenders were identified and taken into custody
Retail theft continues to have a significant impact on businesses, employees, and consumers, locally, and across the province. Beyond the immediate financial losses, these offences also contribute to increased operating costs, safety concerns for retail staff, and reduced quality of life within the community. Initiatives such as this enforcement blitz are designed not only to arrest offenders but also to deter future criminal activity and strengthen relationships between police and the retail sector.
WRPS encourages retailers, employees, and members of the public to promptly report any incidents of theft, shoplifting, or suspicious activity. Timely reporting enables officers to respond effectively, identify offenders, and support ongoing investigations that contribute to safer communities throughout Waterloo Region.
WRPS continues to work closely with the Retail Council of Canada- National Retail Crime Taskforce (RCC) and other retail partners to combat retail and organized crime.

Waterloo Regional Police are reminding the public to stay vigilant following a distraction theft in Kitchener.
On July 23, 2026, at approximately 11:40 a.m., unknown suspects were travelling in a black Volkswagen on Newbury Drive. The driver conducted a U-turn and stopped on the roadway in front of a residence. The vehicle was occupied by a male driver and a female passenger seated in the rear.
The suspects exited the vehicle and asked a passerby for directions to a nearby Portuguese grocery store. The witness was unable to assist, and the victim subsequently approached the vehicle to provide directions. During the conversation, the female suspect offered the victim a gift as a token of appreciation for their assistance. The female suspect then placed her arms around the victims and put a gold-coloured chain around the victim’s neck while also giving them a gold-coloured ring.
At approximately 11:45 a.m., following the interaction, the driver abruptly reversed on Newbury Drive before fleeing at a high rate of speed. The vehicle then turned onto Rolling Meadows Drive and was last seen travelling toward Westheights Drive.
During the interaction, the victim became distracted, at which time their own gold necklace was removed and replaced with the items provided by the suspects. The victim did not sustain any physical injuries.
Investigators are looking to identify and speak to the owner and occupants of the vehicle in the photos below.
The investigation remains ongoing by WRPS' General Investigations Unit.
Anyone with information, including video or dash camera footage from the area at the time of the incident, is asked to contact police at 519-570-9777, extension 4496.
Public Safety Reminder
Waterloo Regional Police have received numerous reports of distraction thefts throughout the region. These incidents occur when suspects deliberately distract victims in order to steal valuables, often within a matter of seconds and without the victim realizing the theft has occurred until after the suspects have left.
Suspects often work in pairs or groups, with one person engaging the victim while another commits the theft. Common tactics include asking for directions, offering assistance or unsolicited gifts such as jewellery, and engaging in overly friendly conversation while invading personal space. These incidents commonly occur in parking lots, shopping areas, and residential neighbourhoods.
While anyone can be targeted, suspects often focus on individuals who are:
Alone
Distracted
Wearing visible valuables
Older adults
Members of the public are encouraged to remain aware of their surroundings, keep personal belongings secure, and avoid allowing strangers into their personal space or accepting unsolicited items. If something feels suspicious, leave the area immediately.
If you believe you have been targeted or victimized, move to a safe location and contact police right away. Do not confront the suspect and, if possible, provide a description of the individual(s) and any associated vehicle.
Distraction thefts rely on catching people off guard. Remaining alert and cautious is the best way to prevent becoming a victim.

Beginning in the summer of 2025, Waterloo Regional Police received numerous reports of home renovation fraud targeting seniors throughout Waterloo Region. In some instances, the victim was also approached by a male posing as a law enforcement officer to further facilitate the fraud.
Victims across the region lost more than $500,000, and investigators have linked the scams to similar incidents reported across Canada.
As a result of the investigation, on July 8, 2026, three males have been arrested and remanded in custody.
Investigators have observed that renovation fraud schemes of this nature are often linked to organized criminal networks that operate across multiple jurisdictions in Canada. In some cases, individuals connected to these networks travel from outside the country and move between communities targeting homeowners, particularly seniors, using deceptive sales tactics and high-pressure contracts.
Waterloo Regional Police continue to work with law enforcement partners across Canada to identify those responsible, disrupt organized criminal activity, and prevent further victimization.
To help protect yourself from renovation fraud, consider the following tips:
Obtain multiple written quotes before committing to any work.
Verify the contractor’s credentials, references, and business history. Do not rely solely on what you find on the company website or social media.
Ensure a detailed written contract is in place before any work begins.
Be cautious of contractors who use high-pressure sales tactics or demand immediate decisions.
Never pay the full cost of a project upfront, especially if the contractor approached you unsolicited. Consider making payments in stages as work is completed and verified.

Waterloo Regional Police are reminding Cambridge residents to lock their vehicles and remove valuables following a series of thefts from vehicles and attempted vehicle entries reported throughout the city over the past month.
Between June 30 and July 24, 2026, WRPS officers investigated 43 incidents involving thefts from vehicles and attempted vehicle entries at residential addresses across Cambridge.
Investigators identified several areas with higher concentrations of incidents, including:
Concession Road area between Eagle Street North and Langs Drive, where nine incidents were reported
Franklin Boulevard and Winston Boulevard area, where five incidents were reported
Arthur Fach Drive and Coulthard Boulevard, where five incidents were reported
Many of the incidents occurred overnight, with suspects targeting vehicles parked in residential driveways. Investigators have determined that a significant number of the vehicles involved had been left unlocked.
“These incidents highlight how thefts from vehicles are often crimes of opportunity,” said Staff Sergeant Jay MacSween of the Waterloo Regional Police Service's South Division Crime Suppression, Analysis, and Response (CSAR) Unit. “Taking a few seconds to lock your vehicle, remove valuables, and secure personal information can significantly reduce your chances of becoming a victim.”
In response, Waterloo Regional Police have launched a two-week Lock It or Lose It campaign running from July 30 to August 13, 2026.
As part of the campaign, members of the South Division CSAR Unit and Waterloo Regional Police Auxiliary members will attend neighbourhoods affected by these incidents to promote crime prevention. Officers and Auxiliary members will distribute educational materials and engage with residents about vehicle security.
Waterloo Regional Police encourage residents to:
Lock all unoccupied vehicles
Remove valuables from vehicles or keep them out of sight
Take wallets, purses, keys, electronics, and identification documents inside
Never leave bank cards, financial information, or personal identification in a vehicle
Report suspicious persons or activity in their neighbourhood immediately

title: Waterloo Regional Police Encourage Awareness of Smart Tracking Technology
content:

Waterloo Regional Police are encouraging residents to be aware of smart tracking devices and their potential misuse following reports of unidentified trackers being discovered on personal property and vehicles.
Bluetooth tracking devices are commonly used to help located personal items such as keys, wallets, luggage, and other valuables. By using Bluetooth technology and nearby mobile devices, these trackers can provide location updates and assist owners in recovering misplace property. While these devices offer many practical benefits, investigators have seen an increase in reports of tracking devices being places on vehicles and personal belongings without the owner's knowledge or consent.
These devices can be misused to monitor an individual's movements and daily activities without their knowledge. By tracking where a vehicle is parked, when someone leaves for work, or when a residence is vacant, offenders may identify opportunities to commit crimes such as vehicle theft, theft from vehicles, break and enters, and other criminal offences.
Trackers can be concealed in a variety of locations on or inside a vehicle, including underneath the vehicle, behind licence plates, within trailer hitch assemblies, inside wheel wells, or among personal belongings or other items stored in or around the vehicle.
Investigators understand that discovering an unfamiliar tracking device can be unsettling. While there may be legitimate reasons for a device's presence in some situations, police encourage residents to treat any unknown tracker seriously and report it to police so the circumstance can be investigated.
Residents are encouraged to periodically inspect their vehicles and personal belongings for unfamiliar devices and to pay attention to smartphone alerts that may indicate an unknown tracking device is moving with them.
If you locate a smart tracking device:
Contact police as soon as possible.
Avoid handling, removing, or disabling the device if possible.
Note when and where the device was discovered.
Be prepared to provide investigators with information that may assist in determining why the device was placed there.
Waterloo Regional Police continue to investigate reports involving unauthorized tracking devices and encourage anyone who discovers an unfamiliar tracker to contact police at 519-570-9777.

Waterloo Regional Police are warning residents and businesses about a fraud scheme involving e-transfers and auto-deposit banking features after investigating a recent incident in North Dumfries Township.
In early August 2026, police received a report that an organization's billing email account had been compromised. Investigators learned that the email address associated with the organization's bank account had been fraudulently reassigned to a separate bank account controlled by an unknown individual.
As a result, e-transfers sent by legitimate clients were successfully processed but were redirected to the fraudulent account rather than being deposited into the intended account.
The fraudulent activity is believed to have occurred between July 30 and August 4, 2026. Once auto-deposit was disabled, the unauthorized redirection of funds stopped.
Investigators believe this method could impact both individuals and businesses that use auto-deposit for e-transfers. The scheme may be difficult to detect, as senders often receive confirmation that funds have been transferred, while the intended recipient never receives the payment.
Waterloo Regional Police are reminding the public to:
Regularly monitor bank accounts and transaction histories.
Review any email addresses associated with auto-deposit features.
Enable multi-factor authentication on email and banking accounts where available.
Investigate unexpected account changes or suspicious activity immediately.
Follow up with recipients of e-transfers to confirm payments have been received.
The investigation remains ongoing.
Anyone who believes they may have been a victim of a similar fraud is encouraged to contact Waterloo Regional Police at 519-570-9777.

On August 13, 2026, members of the WRPS’ Drugs and Firearms Unit arrested a 20-year-old Cambridge male as part of an investigation into the exportation of cocaine from Canada to Hong Kong. The investigation began in September 2025 after a 20-year-old Cambridge female was arrested by authorities in Hong Kong.

Export a Schedule I Substance
Conspiracy to Commit an Indictable Offence
The accused was held in police custody for a bail hearing.

PREVIOUS MEDIA RELEASE:
Waterloo Regional Police have arrested an individual in an ongoing drug investigation.
In September 2025, members of the WRPS’ Drugs and Firearms Unit launched an investigation into cocaine trafficking from Canada to Hong Kong after a 20-year-old Cambridge female was arrested at the Hong Kong International Airport with 25 kilograms of suspected cocaine hidden in her checked luggage.
As a result of an extended investigation and with the support from multiple law enforcement partners, investigators completed a search warrant in Markham on June 11, 2026. A male was arrested in connection with a sophisticated drug network that facilitated her travel from Toronto to Hong Kong.
As a result of the investigation, the 36-year-old Markham male was charged with:
Possession for the purpose of trafficking
Possession for the purpose of exportation
The accused was held for a bail hearing.
The investigation is ongoing.

Waterloo Regional Police Service's Traffic Services Unit is investigating a serious collision involving a motorcycle and a motor vehicle in Kitchener.

title: Waterloo Regional Police Remind Public to Secure Valuables Following Thefts from Vehicles

WA26119144
•

Tuesday, August 18, 2026 7:28 a.m.
Waterloo Regional Police are reminding residents to secure valuables and remove personal information from their vehicles following reports of thefts from vehicles in Waterloo Region.
On August 13, 2026, police received multiple reports of vehicles being entered in heavily populated employee parking lots.
Investigators have learned that wallets and other valuables were targeted during these incidents. In addition to the immediate loss of property, stolen identification and financial cards can be used to facilitate further fraud and identity-related offences.
The incidents are part of a larger, multi-jurisdictional investigation involving police services across Ontario. Since July 2026, investigators have identified nearly 30 victims connected to similar occurrences.
Police are reminding the public to take the following precautions:
Do not leave wallets, purses, identification, financial cards, cash, or other valuables inside your vehicle.
Remove all valuables from plain view before leaving your vehicle unattended.
Ensure vehicle doors are locked and windows are closed.
Report suspicious activity immediately.
The investigation remains ongoing.
Anyone with information related to these incidents is asked to contact Waterloo Regional Police at 519-570-9777.

Waterloo Regional Police are investigating an assault involving bear spray in Kitchener.
On August 15, 2026, at approximately 5:05 a.m., police received a report of a male who had been sprayed with bear spray in a parking lot near Charles Street East and Pandora Avenue North.
The victim made their way to a parking lot in the area of Ottawa Street North and Weber Street East, where a bystander contacted emergency services.
Officers located the male suffering from minor injuries to his eyes and face. He received medical treatment and was transported to hospital.
Investigators believe the incident occurred between 4 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. Police are currently seeking to identify and locate the male suspect involved.
The investigation remains ongoing.
Anyone who witnessed the incident or has video footage from the areas is asked to contact Waterloo Regional Police at 519-570-9777.

Waterloo Regional Police are continuing to investigate a series of residential break and enters in Kitchener.
Members of the Waterloo Regional Police Service's Break and Enter, Auto Theft, and Robbery (BEAR) Unit are seeking witnesses and video footage related to incidents that occurred in the Deer Ridge and Newbury Drive areas on August 15, 2026.
Investigators are looking to identify and speak with a person observed in the Deer Ridge neighbourhood at approximately 11:30 a.m. The individual was seen walking through the area, taking photographs of homes and yards.
The individual is described as:
White male
Approximately 40 years old
5’10” to 6’ tall
Short dark brown hair
Wearing a baseball cap, maroon T-shirt, and blue jeans
Investigators are also seeking information regarding a black BMW SUV that was observed in the Deer Ridge Drive area between approximately 5:20 p.m. and 6 p.m. and later in the Newbury Drive area at approximately 8:50 p.m.
As part of the investigation, officers are asking residents and motorists who were in the area and may have dash camera, residential security camera, or other video footage to review their recordings and submit any relevant footage.
